modules.name: Isovist and visibility graph analysis (space syntax)
modules.design_question: Where can people see and be seen in lobbies, sky lobbies, atria and public floors, and how legible and connected are those spaces?
modules.effort: M (8-12 person-days); depthmapXcli cross-check about 2 days; cell caps and two-graph build about 1 day
inputs: Layer 0: floor-plate polygons for tagged public, lobby, sky-lobby and atrium floors only (Polygon2D[])
Layer 0: core, stair and void polygons used as obstacles (Polygon2D[])
Layer 0: program tags (public, cultural/civic, retail, amenity, office, hotel, residential) used to group results
Advanced mode: user-drawn partition segments, each flagged opaque, glazed (visible, not walkable) or open (Segment2D[] with type flag)
Open stairs and voids that link floors (Link[])
Upstream P12-M04: occupied-area mask (optional)
outputs: VGAField (visibility graph at eye height, glass transparent): per-cell connectivity, clustering coefficient, mean shortest path, integration, isovist area, perimeter, occlusivity, level, tag
PermeabilityField (accessibility graph at floor height, glass a barrier): mean shortest path and integration
ZoneStats: percentiles and means per program tag within each connected graph (feeds P12-M05 and boards)
SightLinks: pairs of (entry or lift lobby, public zone) that are mutually visible (feeds MOBI wayfinding)
IsovistPolygons: Polygon2D[] for user-selected viewpoints

parameters.name: Grid spacing
parameters.relationship: A finer grid gives a more faithful field but pair tests grow with cells squared. Turner et al. (2001) used 1.0 m at eye level (Villa Mairea) and 0.5 m on a small pavilion; default 1.0 m, coarser on large floors.

parameters.name: Plan cut / eye height
parameters.relationship: Cut height decides which furniture, balustrades and partitions block sight; a lower cut leaves fewer obstacles and larger isovists. Team preset recorded as a judgement, not a sourced value.

parameters.name: Partition type flag (opaque / glazed / open)
parameters.relationship: A visibility edge exists or not, so no fractions. Glazed is visible but a barrier in the accessibility graph; opaque blocks both; open passes both. Glass raises isovist area and lowers visual privacy.

parameters.name: Analysis radius (local vs global)
parameters.relationship: A small radius emphasises legibility inside one room or lobby; an unlimited radius measures visibility from the whole connected graph. Turner et al. distinguish local and global properties.

parameters.name: Vertical links (atrium, open stair, void)
parameters.relationship: Linking nodes across open stairs, as Turner et al. did at Villa Mairea, merges levels into one connected graph: integration rises for connected floors and falls for isolated ones.

parameters.name: Floors analysed and cell cap
parameters.relationship: Pair tests grow with cells squared: one full-block floor at 1.0 m is about 11,500 cells (about 6.6e7 pairs); 60-80 merged tower floors reach about 1e5 cells (about 1e10 pairs). Analyse tagged public floors only; cap cells; send big jobs to depthmapXcli.

parameters.name: Core position and shape
parameters.relationship: A central core with a ring corridor breaks long sight lines and raises occlusivity at corners; an edge or split core opens deeper views from the lobby (geometric consequence, tested per scheme).

metrics.name: Mean visual integration by program tag and level
metrics.unit: relative index (normalised within each connected graph)
metrics.good: Lobbies, sky lobbies and public floors in the upper quartile of the project's own distribution
metrics.bad: The same zones in the lower quartile
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] No absolute threshold published. Tate Gallery room occupancy fitted mean shortest path length by an exponential curve (R2 = 0.63; Turner et al. 2001): evidence of relative use, not a threshold. Quartile rule is a team preset.
metrics.method: Normalised mean shortest-path length per connected visibility graph; ranks never mixed across graphs

metrics.name: Visual clustering coefficient
metrics.good: Low values at entrances and lift-lobby decision points (multidirectional field); high values acceptable inside enclosed rooms
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Turner et al. (2001) associate low clustering with multidirectional junctions and decision points and high clustering with private rooms (Villa Mairea). The pass rule is a team preset.
metrics.method: Share of a cell's visible neighbours that can see each other

metrics.name: Isovist occlusivity
metrics.good: Below the floor median at entry sequences so destinations are seen on approach
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Definition from isovists.org after Benedikt (1979, full text unopened). Thresholds are team presets; no published numbers found.
metrics.method: Sum of occlusive edges divided by isovist perimeter

metrics.name: Entry / lift-lobby visibility from public floor area
metrics.good: 80% or more (editable preset)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Presets chosen by the team to test wayfinding legibility; no source.
metrics.method: Share of public cells whose isovist contains an entry or lift-lobby node

modules.method: 1) Select tagged public, lobby, sky-lobby and atrium floors; slice each at the cut height. 2) Build two graphs on a 1.0 m grid: a visibility graph at eye height (glass transparent) and an accessibility graph at floor height (glass a barrier), using binary obstacle flags. 3) Link floors only where open stairs or voids connect them. 4) Per cell compute 2D isovist area, perimeter, occlusivity, connectivity, clustering coefficient, mean shortest path and integration (Turner et al. 2001). 5) Normalise integration per connected graph and rank tags within that graph only. 6) Enforce a cell cap; larger jobs run in depthmapXcli as a separate process and are compared with the in-browser field. 7) Optionally correlate with user-supplied movement counts.
visualization: Paired plans per floor: visibility field at eye height and accessibility field at floor height, perceptually uniform ramp, legend shows the project's own min, quartiles and max
Live isovist polygon under the cursor with area, perimeter and occlusivity read-out
Scatter of integration vs connectivity coloured by program tag, brushed to highlight cells on the plan
Vertical strip showing mean integration per connected graph, with sky lobbies and atria marked
modules.human_judgment: Whether high visibility is desirable for a space (public lobby versus private amenity or prayer room); the privacy/prospect-refuge trade-off; which partitions are glass; which zones count as public; how much the human-scale criterion favours legibility over intimacy.
modules.limits: 2D slice at one eye height; furniture, reflections, lighting and human field of view (about 120-180 degrees) are ignored. Massing-only models have no interior partitions, so results mean nothing until a partition layer exists. No absolute thresholds are published: results are relative to the project and to one connected graph. Cost grows with cells squared; a cap applies.

modules.name: View access to mountains, water and landmarks (LEED views and EN 17037 view out)
modules.design_question: Which floors and facades see the North Shore Mountains, Burrard Inlet, Stanley Park and landmarks past neighbouring towers, and do those views meet recognised view levels, given an assumed real location for the hypothetical site?
modules.effort: L (10-14 person-days). First v1 slice (about 5 days): proxy-block azimuth sectors, context ray casting, per-point EN 17037 and LEED view share, sensitivity runs. Later v1: DEM ridgeline, water polygons, panoramas.
depends_on: SITE: georeferenced proxy block and true-north rotation (recorded team assumption)
inputs: Layer 0: floor plates, floor heights and facade faces with outward normals (Mesh, Polygon3D[])
Context massing of existing and approved towers in the 244-305 m range, imported or from open data (Mesh)
SITE packet: georeferenced proxy block, true-north rotation and alternative proxy blocks for sensitivity runs (team assumption)
Target markers from the site plan (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet, North Shore Mountains) converted to azimuth sectors from the proxy block (Point3D / azimuth sector)
Optional: ridgeline polyline from a DEM (HRDEM, OGL-Canada) and water polygons (OSM, ODbL)
Optional from P12-M06: window and spandrel layout (default continuous vision glazing); from P12-M04: regularly occupied zones and use
outputs: ViewPointField: per eye point and level, targets visible, LEED view type, horizontal sight angle, outside distance, layers seen, EN 17037 level
FloorViewTable: per floor and use, % of area with LEED view and by target seen; EN 17037 levels per point with area share labelled a tool convention
PremiumViewFloors: floor ranges seeing both mountains and water (feeds PROG value stacking and P12-M05)
FacadeViewScores: per orientation (feeds P12-M06 WWR decisions)
SensitivityTable: target-view share per proxy block and rotation
ViewPanorama: image strips with ridgeline and water highlighted (feeds PRES boards)

parameters.name: Eye height
parameters.relationship: 1.2 m (seated) and 1.7 m (standing) are team presets; an arXiv summary (unopened) reports both in computational EN 17037 studies. A higher eye point clears sills and furniture, slightly changing layers seen and distance.

parameters.name: Proxy block location and rotation range
parameters.relationship: Target azimuths, ridgeline and water visibility depend on the real block the hypothetical site is assumed to occupy. Moving the proxy or rotating it shifts which floors and faces see each target; all target results are conditional on it.

parameters.name: Context tower height and spacing on the mountain side
parameters.relationship: Taller or closer towers between site and mountains raise the lowest floor that sees the ridgeline and shorten outside distance, so premium-view floors move up.

parameters.name: Facade orientation (true north corrected)
parameters.relationship: A facade whose normal falls inside a target's azimuth sector sees that target; rotating the footprint shifts which faces see mountains or water. The site plan's north arrow is skewed from the street grid.

parameters.name: Floor level
parameters.relationship: Higher floors see over the context and gain a larger visible ridgeline arc and longer outside distance, until the floor is above all neighbours.

parameters.name: Vision glazing width / WWR
parameters.relationship: Wider glazing increases the horizontal sight angle; EN 17037 grades it at 14, 28 and 54 degrees for minimum, medium and high levels.

parameters.name: Target definition and weights
parameters.relationship: User weights decide whether mountain, water or park views dominate the premium-floor ranking; weights are subjective and stored as judgement records.

parameters.name: Ray step and minimum visible fraction
parameters.relationship: A smaller step finds narrow gaps between towers but costs more rays; the minimum fraction decides when a floor 'has' a view of a target. Both are editable presets.

metrics.name: Regularly occupied area with a LEED-style view through vision glazing
metrics.good: 90% or more (3 points) or 75% or more (2 points) under LEED v5 EQc2 Option 1 Path 2
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] LEEDuser quotes v5: 75% (2 pts) or 90% (3 pts), VLT above 40%, view within 3 x head height. USGBC text unopened. v4.1 (CaGBC) and v4 are legacy_version. M02 owns the LEED views result.
metrics.method: Fraction of occupied area whose eye points have an unobstructed ray through vision glazing to a qualifying view type

metrics.name: LEED view type present at each counted point
metrics.good: At least one of nature, urban landmark, art, or objects 7.5 m or more away
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] v5 (LEEDuser) and v4.1 (CaGBC) list these types. Mapping mountain, water and park targets to 'nature' and BC Place-type targets to 'urban landmark' is the team's judgement.
metrics.method: Classify rays: hit on a target polygon (nature, landmark) or on any object 7.5 m or more away

metrics.name: EN 17037 horizontal sight angle (per point)
metrics.good: 28 degrees or more (medium); 54 degrees or more (high)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] REHVA Journal and ClimateStudio give identical table values; standard text unopened. View out is a point-in-space method (Annex C); area share is a software convention.
metrics.method: Total horizontal angle subtended by windows seen from the eye point

metrics.name: EN 17037 outside distance of view (per point)
metrics.good: 20 m or more (medium); 50 m or more (high)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Same two sources. ClimateStudio defines it as the median distance to objects seen through windows. Standard text unopened.
metrics.method: Median ray distance through windows

metrics.name: EN 17037 layers seen (sky, landscape, ground)
metrics.good: 2 layers (medium) to 3 layers (high)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] REHVA gives 1/2/3 layers; ClimateStudio says minimum needs the landscape layer, medium landscape plus one, high all three. Nuance unresolved.
metrics.method: Classify rays through windows as sky, ground or landscape (other objects)

metrics.name: Share of occupied area seeing at least one priority target (mountain ridgeline, water, Stanley Park)
metrics.good: At or above the user's per-use target (placeholder 50%, editable)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] No sourced benchmark. Ulrich (1984) reports better recovery for patients with a natural view; it supports the value of nature views but gives no threshold.
metrics.method: Count eye points with a visible target fraction above the minimum

metrics.name: Target-view share range across proxy-block and rotation runs
metrics.good: Range within the user's stated tolerance (no preset)
metrics.bad: Wider than tolerance: show the result as conditional on the proxy
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] The site is hypothetical; target directions come from site-plan labels, not georeferenced points. The tolerance is a team judgement.
metrics.method: Repeat target tests for alternative proxy blocks and +/- rotation; report min-max

modules.method: 1) Take the SITE packet's georeferenced proxy block and true-north rotation; derive target azimuth sectors; repeat for alternative proxies or +/- rotation (sensitivity). 2) For each level sample eye points at 1.2 m and 1.7 m (team presets) in regularly occupied zones near glazing. 3) Cast rays through each window opening at a preset step against the context mesh (BVH); classify each as sky, ground, landscape or target hit. 4) Per point: sight angle, median outside distance, layers; EN 17037 level = worst of three. 5) LEED: share of occupied area with a clear ray to a qualifying view type. 6) Later v1: ridgeline test (ray elevation above DEM samples) and water test (sea-level plane inside water polygons). 7) Aggregate by floor, facade and use; label area shares a tool convention and every target result 'conditional on proxy'.
visualization: Unrolled facade 'view matrix': x = true-north azimuth, y = floor level, colour = target seen (mountain, water, park, none) with the context skyline overlaid and a 'conditional on proxy' stamp
Plan map per level in four categorical colours: fail, minimum, medium, high EN 17037 level per point (fixed legend, clause linked)
Panorama strip from a chosen floor with ridgeline and water highlighted, exportable for boards
Stacked bar of % area by use with LEED view result and view types, shown as reference line until the source is verified
modules.human_judgment: Which views matter and why (mountains and water as place-based and Indigenous relationships to land); how to weigh premium view against glare, solar gain and privacy, including overlook between towers; whether to orient a tower to a view or shelter the public realm; how culturally significant views appear on boards; which proxy block is plausible.
modules.limits: Results are conditional on the assumed proxy block and on context massing; approved-but-unbuilt towers are uncertain. Trees, haze and reflections are ignored. EN 17037 is a European standard and LEED a voluntary credit, neither a Vancouver requirement; tiers rate window geometry, not scenic value. HRDEM coverage of North Shore ridgelines is unverified. Public view cones protect views from public places, not from inside the tower.

modules.name: Depth from glazing, daylight reach and glare (CLIM ingest)
modules.design_question: How far is each regularly occupied area from the nearest vision glazing, and does the plate stay within recognised daylight, view-proximity and glare levels?
modules.effort: S-M (4-6 person-days); glare ingest adds about 1 day
depends_on: CLIM daylight outputs (sDA, ASE, DGP), optional
inputs: Layer 0: floor-plate and core polygons per level (Polygon2D[])
Layer 0: floor-to-floor height; program tags
P12-M06: glazing segments, window head height, visible light transmittance (FacadeSchedule)
P12-M04: regularly occupied area mask
Optional CLIM packet: sDA, ASE, illuminance and DGP/DGPe rasters per level
outputs: DepthField: distance-to-glazing raster per level
DeepPlanZones: polygons beyond the chosen reach (feeds P12-M04 reallocation to storage, core, MEP or non-regular occupancy)
OccupiableAreaStats: % of occupied area per distance band (feeds ENER lighting and daylight controls)
DaylightComplianceFlags: per level result against cited tests, shown as reference lines until sources are verified
GlareFlags: perimeter zones above the DGPe levels (feeds P12-M06 shading)

parameters.name: Window head height
parameters.relationship: LEED counts unobstructed views within 3 x head height of vision glazing, so higher heads enlarge the area that counts; taller floor-to-floor also adds facade area and cost.

parameters.name: Plate depth (glazing-to-core dimension)
parameters.relationship: A wider plate or larger core increases the share of floor beyond reach, shrinking the share of occupied area inside the 3 x head-height and 6 m bands (geometric consequence).

parameters.name: Core location and split
parameters.relationship: A central core leaves a perimeter ring of depth (half plate width minus half core width); a side or split core makes single-sided deep plates. Both change the distance field directly.

parameters.name: Vision glazing transmittance (VLT)
parameters.relationship: LEED v4.1 and v5 pages quote 40% or more for view glazing; tinted or fritted glass lowers VLT and the daylight reaching deeper zones.

parameters.name: Interior surface reflectance (from P12-M07 lightness)
parameters.relationship: Daylight factor adds an internally reflected component, so lighter ceilings and walls push usable daylight deeper.

parameters.name: External obstruction angle (neighbouring towers)
parameters.relationship: Closer or taller neighbours reduce the sky component at lower floors, shortening usable daylight reach regardless of plan depth.

parameters.name: Lighting-control daylight-zone factor k (zone depth = k x head height)
parameters.relationship: Larger k classes more of the plate as daylit. k = 2.0 mirrors ASHRAE 90.1 primary plus secondary sidelighted areas (one head height each), a lighting-control convention, not a daylight-adequacy test; simulated sDA replaces it.

parameters.name: Shading depth and glazing (from P12-M06)
parameters.relationship: Deeper shading or lower transmittance lowers DGPe at the facade but also cuts view and daylight; the effect is simulated in CLIM, not computed here.

metrics.name: Occupied area within 3 x head height of vision glazing (diagnostic for the M02 LEED views result)
metrics.good: 75% or more (reference line)
metrics.basis: [proxy] LEED v4/v4.1 views test counts unobstructed views within 3 x head height; v5 repeats it (LEEDuser). Reading it as an area share is the team's interpretation. M02 owns the badge; M03 only explains it.
metrics.method: Raster area inside the 3 x head-height band divided by occupied area

metrics.name: Occupied area within 6 m of envelope glazing (LEED v5 EQc2 Option 5 Path 3)
metrics.good: 30% or more, with glazing VLT above 40%
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] LEEDuser quotes v5 Path 3 (1 pt): at least 30% of regularly occupied area within 20 ft (6 m) of envelope glazing. USGBC text unopened.
metrics.method: Raster area within 6 m of vision glazing divided by occupied area

metrics.name: Spatial daylight autonomy sDA (ingested from CLIM)
metrics.good: 75% or more (top of v5 scale, 4 pts; v4 3 pts)
metrics.basis: [legacy_version] LEEDuser: v5 averages sDA300/50% or sDA150/50% (IES LM-83-23), 40% = 1 pt to 75% = 4 pts; v4 gave 55% = 2 pts, 75% = 3 pts. USGBC v5 text unopened.
metrics.method: Read simulated raster; compute area above 300 lx (or 150 lx) for 50% of hours

metrics.name: Annual sunlight exposure ASE1000,250 (ingested from CLIM)
metrics.good: At or below 10% (v4 reference); at or below 20% with no glare explanation (v5 as quoted)
metrics.bad: Above 10% (v4); above 20% needs a glare explanation (v5)
metrics.basis: [legacy_version] v4 EQc7 Option 1 limit 10%; LEEDuser quotes v5: spaces with ASE above 20% must explain glare treatment. USGBC v5 text unopened.
metrics.method: Area above 1000 lx for 250 or more occupied hours

metrics.name: EN 17037 daylight provision (ingested from CLIM)
metrics.good: 300 lx over 50% of the plane and 100 lx over 95% (minimum); 500/300 (medium); 750/500 (high)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] REHVA Journal summary of the EN 17037 table; targets hold for half of daylight hours (2190 h). Standard text unopened.
metrics.method: Read simulated illuminance raster; compute area fractions

metrics.name: EN 17037 glare protection, DGPe (ingested from CLIM)
metrics.good: Below 0.35 (high), 0.40 (medium) or 0.45 (minimum)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] REHVA table lists DGPe below 0.45/0.40/0.35. Time and view-direction conditions and the standard text were not read. Ingested from CLIM, not computed here.
metrics.method: Read simulated DGP/DGPe at occupied eye points; compare with levels

metrics.name: Distance to glazing against lighting-control zone depth (proxy)
metrics.good: At or below k x head height with k = 2.0 (editable)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] k = 2.0 mirrors ASHRAE 90.1 sidelighted areas (draft addendum text seen, unopened). Reinhart (2005) abstract: simulations largely support the head-height rule for standard variants. k stays a preset until sDA replaces it.
metrics.method: Euclidean or visibility distance from each occupied cell to the nearest glazing segment

modules.method: 1) Rasterise each floor at 0.5 m; mask core, voids and non-occupied tags. 2) Compute distance from each occupied cell to the nearest vision-glazing segment (Euclidean distance transform; optionally limited to cells with a sight line using P12-M01). 3) Classify cells into bands: within 3 x head height (diagnostic), within 6 m (LEED v5 proximity), within k x head height (lighting-control proxy), beyond. 4) Report area shares per level and use. 5) Ingest CLIM sDA, ASE, illuminance and DGP rasters; overlay and test against the cited levels; show disagreements with the proxy. 6) Output deep-plan polygons for reallocation and glare flags for P12-M06 shading. The LEED views result stays in P12-M02.
visualization: Plan heat map per level: distance-to-glazing contours at 3 m steps with the 3 x head-height line, 6 m line and k x head-height line drawn bold
Section sketch showing head height, 3 x head-height reach and k x head-height reach
Floor-by-floor bar of % occupied area in each band with the reference lines
Toggle overlay of simulated sDA and DGPe rasters against the geometric proxy
modules.human_judgment: Whether a deep zone is acceptable for its use (trading floor, meeting rooms, hotel corridor); whether an atrium or light well compensates; occupant preference for views versus density; the trade-off against core efficiency; how much glare control to accept at the cost of view.
modules.limits: A distance proxy, not a daylight simulation: it ignores sky condition (Vancouver winter overcast), orientation, obstruction, glazing and shading. k is a team preset. LEED and EN 17037 values come from secondary pages and v4 values are legacy; both are voluntary benchmarks, not VBBL requirements. Hotel and residential units need room-level depth rules.

modules.name: Activity-based program: occupancy bases, schedules and people counts
modules.design_question: How many people use each activity at each hour, and which population (egress, design, energy, vertical transportation) should egress, elevators and energy modules use?
modules.effort: M (6-8 person-days) including area-basis tags and the fourth basis
inputs: Layer 0: gross area per program tag and floor (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public, amenity, mechanical, core, below-grade)
Unit counts: hotel keys, dwelling units, bedrooms and sleeping rooms
Area-basis tag for each density (GFA, zone floor area, net usable)
Activity-setting table: workstations, collaboration, focus, meeting, amenity, dining, assembly, with user-sourced densities
Workplace-strategy inputs: attendance factor, utilisation scenario, event-load multipliers
Optional P12-M03: occupied-area share after deep-plan reallocation
outputs: PopulationTable: persons by floor x use x basis (egress, design, energy, vertical transportation), each with its area basis, typed for SYST egress and lifts
HourlySchedule: occupancy fraction by use x day type x hour (feeds ENER internal gains and ventilation)
PeakCoincident: coincident peak population by core, lift bank and stair (feeds SYST)
TripGenerationInputs: arrivals and departures by hour (feeds MOBI)
FSRRange: non-residential FSR, strict and inclusive counts, with the toggles used

parameters.name: Area basis of each density (GFA / zone floor area / net usable)
parameters.relationship: DOE/PNNL densities are per zone floor area, not net usable area. Applying a net-to-gross factor to them understates population; the tag decides whether efficiency applies.

parameters.name: Net-to-gross efficiency by use (net-basis densities only)
parameters.relationship: Higher efficiency leaves more net area per gross, raising population only for net-basis densities. No sourced Vancouver supertall values found (unresolved).

parameters.name: Occupant density by activity and basis
parameters.relationship: Lower m2/person raises persons per floor, so egress width, lift demand, ventilation and gains. Four bases stay apart: egress (code), design, energy and vertical transportation; energy density never feeds lifts.

parameters.name: Persons per sleeping room and dwelling
parameters.relationship: Egress uses 2 persons per bedroom or sleeping area (VBBL 2019 Part 9 text; Part 3 wording to verify). Design and energy use DOE 1.5 per hotel room and 2.5 per apartment, changing populations without changing area.

parameters.name: Attendance / desk-sharing factor (design, energy, vertical bases only)
parameters.relationship: Lower attendance reduces average and sometimes peak office population, lowering energy gains and lift demand. Egress stays at 1.0; every change is logged as a judgement.

parameters.name: Activity-setting densities and utilisation scenario
parameters.unit: m2 per person by setting; % utilisation
parameters.relationship: Per-setting densities (desk, collaboration, focus, amenity) and a utilisation scenario change design and energy populations only; each change is a judgement record. Egress keeps 1.0.

parameters.name: Lift-planning density and five-minute handling target
parameters.unit: m2 per person (net); % of population per 5 min
parameters.relationship: Lift demand follows the vertical basis. Reference points: 10, 14 and 19 m2 per person; 15% historic versus about 6-7% surveyed peak. CIBSE Guide D not opened.

parameters.name: Hourly schedule fractions
parameters.relationship: Peak hours that differ between uses (office, hotel, retail) spread demand in shared cores; sums of peaks overstate simultaneous population.

parameters.name: Event-load multiplier for cultural/assembly space
parameters.relationship: Scheduled events lift population above the typical day and can govern egress and lift sizing for public floors.

parameters.name: FSR counting toggles (strict or inclusive)
parameters.relationship: Counting only office and retail/commercial gives the strict FSR; adding hotel or cultural/civic raises it by their area. Each toggle needs a judgement record; mechanical, core and below-grade are excluded by default.

metrics.name: Design occupant density by activity (reference)
metrics.unit: m2 per person (zone floor area basis)
metrics.good: Uses the reference value or a documented, sourced override
metrics.basis: [legacy_version] PNNL scorecard, 90.1-2004 rows, Buffalo, per zone floor area: office 18.58; hotel room 26.01 and 16.35; lobby 3.1; retail 6.19; dining 1.33; apartment 35.3. Energy-model loads, not VBBL values, not for lifts.
metrics.method: Lookup by program tag and zone type

metrics.name: Egress-basis population against VBBL occupant load
metrics.good: Egress sized to the larger of the VBBL table load and the egress-basis designed number
metrics.bad: Sized to the table load while the designed number is larger
metrics.basis: [unverified] VBBL 2025 Part 3 Table 3.1.17.1 and Article 3.1.17.1 not read. VBBL 2019 Part 9 text: designed number, not fewer than the table. Office factor 9.3 m2/person is recalled, unverified.
metrics.method: Compute both loads per floor; show the larger; flag floors where design exceeds table

metrics.name: Non-residential (employment) FSR, strict and inclusive
metrics.unit: FSR on a site of about 11,468 m2 (79.2 x 144.8 m)
metrics.good: Strict count (office plus retail/commercial) at or above 9.0 (about 103,200 m2); inclusive count shown as a separate bar
metrics.bad: Strict count below 9.0 even if the inclusive count passes
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] 9.0 FSR of non-residential, high-employment (office, commercial) floor area is the team's summary of the VTC brief; brief PDF not opened. Floor-area definition and Vancouver exclusions unresolved.
metrics.method: Sum strict-tag area divided by site area; add toggled tags for the inclusive bar; exclude mechanical, core, below-grade by default

metrics.name: Implied persons per key / dwelling (design basis)
metrics.good: Matches reference (hotel 1.5, dwelling 2.5) or a documented override
metrics.basis: [legacy_version] Derived from PNNL scorecard room area divided by m2 per person (39.02/26.01 and 88.25/35.3), 90.1-2004 rows. Egress uses 2 persons per sleeping area instead.
metrics.method: Rooms x persons per room

metrics.name: Vertical-transportation population basis
metrics.good: Documented values stated against 10-19 m2 per person and 7-15% references
metrics.bad: Energy-basis density reused for lifts, or undocumented values
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] Designing Buildings wiki summarises BCO and NAO densities and the Stanhope 2004 survey (6% observed morning peak). CIBSE Guide D (2025) not opened.
metrics.method: Population = net area / density x attendance; handling target applied by lift bank

modules.method: Per (floor, tag, activity): N = area x density x attendance, with each density's area basis tagged; apply net-to-gross only to net-basis densities. Four bases: egress = larger of the VBBL table load and the designed number (attendance 1.0; dwellings and hotels at 2 persons per sleeping area x bedrooms); design = DOE/PNNL density or sourced override; energy = design population x ASHRAE 90.1-derived schedules; vertical transportation = lift-planning density and five-minute handling target. Aggregate by core, lift bank, stair and hour with a coincidence factor. FSR: strict = office plus retail/commercial area; inclusive adds hotel and cultural/civic by toggle; exclude mechanical, core and below-grade by default; show both. Never feed the energy density to lifts. Export typed tables.
visualization: Vertical people profile: horizontal stacked bars per floor by use, with a basis toggle (egress, design, energy, vertical transportation)
24 h x use heat map of schedule fractions for weekday, weekend and event day
Waterfall from GFA to zone area to net area to people for each basis, showing both area bases
FSR bars: strict versus inclusive against 9.0, with toggles listed
Badge row linking each density and schedule to its source row or clause
modules.human_judgment: The workplace strategy (activity-based working, desk sharing, hybrid attendance); whether to design for code maxima or expected use; which uses count towards the 9.0 FSR; tenant mix; hotel and household sizes; how public and cultural programs are used across day and year.
modules.limits: Reference densities are US prototype loads (2004 rows) and lift-planning figures are secondary; neither is a Vancouver tower survey, and post-2020 hybrid work is not captured. The VBBL table and area basis must be read by a professional before use. This is not a code check; the brief says its documents are not legal documents.

modules.name: Adjacency matrix and vertical stacking
modules.design_question: Which uses must sit near or apart from each other, and does the vertical stack of public, office, hotel, residential and mechanical floors satisfy those relationships, the physical drivers of a mixed-use supertall and the brief?
depends_on: SYST/STRC: floor-to-floor heights, cores, transfer and outrigger floors
inputs: Layer 0: program blocks (tag x floor range) with areas
User relationship ratings per pair of uses (entered in the matrix)
P12-M04: schedules and populations (peak-hour overlap, shared lift demand)
SYST/STRC: core and shaft locations, floor-to-floor height by use, transfer and outrigger floors
P12-M03: plate depth by use
outputs: AdjacencyMatrix: typed pair ratings with author and rationale
StackingOrder: floor-range sequence with two score sets (subjective ratings; physical checks)
ConflictList: violated pairs, shared-core conflicts, schedule overlaps, stack-alignment and entry-path conflicts (feeds SYST lift zoning, MOBI servicing, P12-M01)

parameters.name: Closeness rating per use pair (A, E, I, O, U, X)
parameters.relationship: Higher ratings force pairs closer or onto a shared core; X forces separation. A ('absolutely necessary') and X ('necessary to keep apart') appear on a lecture page; E, I, O, U meanings are team presets. Muther's text not opened.

parameters.name: Vertical distance between related uses
parameters.relationship: More floors between related uses lowers the pair's satisfaction and raises vertical travel; a shared sky lobby can shorten effective distance.

parameters.name: Schedule overlap between uses on a shared lift bank
parameters.relationship: More overlap raises simultaneous demand on shared lifts and lobbies and raises the conflict score.

parameters.name: Public-use continuity
parameters.relationship: The VTC brief (team summary) wants public-facing uses to extend vertically; a longer gap lowers the continuity score and flags podium-only public programs.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor height by use
parameters.relationship: Office, hotel, residential and cultural floors need different heights; mixing them changes stack height and where transfers fall. Values come from SYST/STRC, not set here.

parameters.name: Plate or lease depth by use
parameters.relationship: Deep office plates versus shallow hotel and residential plates decide where each use can sit; a mismatch forces setbacks or transfer floors.

parameters.name: Stack alignment (wet stacks, columns, shafts, transfer and outrigger floors)
parameters.relationship: Misaligned wet stacks, columns or shafts between uses add transfer structure and MEP offsets; transfer and outrigger floors are fixed floors in the search.

parameters.name: Separate entry, lobby and lift path per use
parameters.unit: count of uses with own path
parameters.relationship: Hotel, residential, office and cultural uses normally need separate entries and lift banks; a shared path raises conflicts, lift demand and security issues.

parameters.name: Separation requirements between major occupancies
parameters.relationship: VBBL separations add slab and shaft constraints between hotel, residential and office floors; values are not in the tool until the by-law is read (unresolved).

metrics.name: Count of X-rated pairs that are adjacent or share a core
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] X means 'necessary to keep apart' in the chart, so zero is success by definition; the pairs themselves are subjective.
metrics.method: Check pair distance against the X rule

metrics.name: Share of A-rated pairs satisfied
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] A means 'absolutely necessary'; satisfaction means within the distance the user set for A pairs.
metrics.method: Count A pairs within their distance limit

metrics.name: Weighted adjacency score
metrics.good: 0.8 or more (editable)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Weights and cut-offs are team presets; the chart is qualitative and comes from factory layout practice.
metrics.method: Sum of rating weight x proximity over pairs, divided by the maximum

metrics.name: Vertical continuity of public-facing uses
metrics.good: Public-tagged floors in base, mid and upper tower zones
metrics.bad: Public uses only in the podium
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] VTC brief (team summary, PDF unopened) says public-facing uses should extend vertically; the gap limit is the team's reading.
metrics.method: Largest run of floors with no public-facing tag

metrics.name: Uses with their own entry and lift path
metrics.good: Every use has its own path
metrics.bad: Any use shares a path with an incompatible use
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Team rule from mixed-use tower practice; no source opened. Scored apart from the subjective ratings.
metrics.method: Check lobby, entry and lift-bank assignment per use

metrics.name: Stack-alignment conflicts
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Wet-stack, column and shaft alignment between uses and transfer-floor positions; thresholds are the team's and need SYST/STRC input.
metrics.method: Compare shaft and stack positions between adjacent use blocks

metrics.name: Plate-depth fit by use
metrics.good: Within the user-set depth range for each use
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] No sourced plate-depth ranges; the user sets them from P12-M03 and SYST results.
metrics.method: Compare plate depth per floor range with the range for its use

modules.method: 1) Define program blocks from Layer 0 tags and floor ranges. 2) Show a triangular relationship chart; the user rates each pair with a short reason, stored as a judgement record. 3) Convert ratings to weights; compute proximity from floor distance and shared-core membership. 4) Score subjective items (pair ratings, A and X rules, public continuity) separately from physical checks (floor-to-floor height, plate depth, wet-stack and transfer alignment, own entry and lift path per use, schedule overlap from P12-M04). 5) Optionally search stack orders (simulated annealing) with fixed floors (mechanical, transfer, outrigger, sky lobbies). 6) Output the matrix, both score sets and a conflict list. No rating weights are sourced; all are editable.
visualization: Triangular relationship chart with rating colours and satisfied/violated outlines
Tower section with coloured program blocks and arcs between related blocks; X pairs in red; transfer and outrigger floors marked
Conflict list with links to the pair's recorded rationale, split into subjective and physical
Side-by-side comparison of two stack variants
modules.human_judgment: All pair ratings; acceptable exceptions and justified breaches; operator needs (hotel sky lobby, residential privacy); where cultural and civic programs sit and what community engagement says; priorities between public benefit and commercial stacking.
modules.limits: Ratings have no empirical basis and come from factory layout practice. Floor heights, plate depths, outriggers and MEP zones come from other packets. VBBL separations between major occupancies were not read. The score ranks options; it does not prove one better.

modules.name: Facade and envelope: WWR, shading, thermal performance, bird-friendly glazing
modules.design_question: How much glazing, shading and thermal performance does each facade orientation need, and does the glass treatment meet bird-friendly and view requirements for a 300 m tower on the Pacific Flyway?
modules.effort: M (6-8 person-days). Core cut (about 4 days): WWR by orientation, bird-collision-zone quantities and treated share, VLT check. v1: fly-through and corner checks, shading and U-value roll-up.
inputs: Layer 0: facade faces with area, outward normal and true-north rotation; floor heights
Parametric facade module: bay width, spandrel height, mullion width, glazing split (or user-drawn facade)
P12-M02: view score per orientation
CLIM (optional): incident radiation, sDA and DGP per facade
ECOL (optional): heights and positions of trees, green roofs, sky gardens, podium planting and water features near glass
Glazing and opaque assembly properties from P12-M07 or the user (U, SHGC, VLT, effective U)
outputs: FacadeSchedule: face id, orientation, gross area, glazing area, WWR, glazing U/SHGC/VLT, bird treatment (feeds P12-M07, ENER, cost)
BirdZoneReport: collision-zone glass area, treated area (overhang credit shown), share, pattern spacing, fly-through and corner conditions, night-lighting flag (feeds ECOL)
EnvelopeModel: honeybee JSON or gbXML (feeds ENER modelling against the City's TEUI/TEDI/GHGI metrics)
ShadingGeometry: devices as Mesh (feeds CLIM)
WindowOpenings: segments with head height (feeds P12-M02 and P12-M03)

parameters.name: WWR per orientation and floor band
parameters.relationship: Higher WWR increases daylight and views but also solar gain, conductive loss and glazing embodied carbon, and raises glass area in the bird zone. Optimal WWR is climate-dependent (Goia 2016, European climates; not opened).

parameters.name: Glazing U-factor, SHGC and VLT
parameters.relationship: Lower SHGC cuts cooling load but usually lowers VLT, trading against daylight and the 40% VLT quoted for LEED view glazing; lower U cuts heat loss and radiant asymmetry.

parameters.name: Opaque assembly effective U with thermal bridging
parameters.relationship: Slab edges, balconies and curtain-wall transitions reduce effective insulation, so a nominal U understates heat loss; the BC Housing Thermal Envelope database supplies bridging scenarios.

parameters.name: Shading depth and fin spacing
parameters.relationship: Deeper overhangs or closer fins cut solar gain and glare on south and west faces but reduce view angle and daylight and add structure and cost; effect comes from CLIM.

parameters.name: Bird-collision zone height (local to vegetation)
parameters.unit: m above grade or above local vegetation
parameters.relationship: UBC: treat glazing up to 16 m or 4 m above the tallest vegetation, whichever is greater; a CSA summary says 16-25 m. For sky gardens the vegetation rule applies locally around each planted area (team reading), not as one tower-wide height.

parameters.name: Marker spacing and pattern type
parameters.relationship: Tighter markers are more visible to birds but cut visible clear area; markers 50 mm apart or closer follow the '2 x 2 rule' in the CSA summary.

parameters.name: Fly-through conditions and glass corners
parameters.relationship: Parallel panes and glass corners create an apparent void birds fly through; UBC requires eliminating them and treating corners 5 m each direction, so they add treated area and constrain corner glazing.

parameters.name: Overhang credit
parameters.unit: ratio of shaded area counted as treated
parameters.relationship: UBC, citing CSA A460-2019, counts overhang shading as treated area up to 1:1, less effective than markers; it lowers the glass needing patterns but adds structure and cost.

parameters.name: Exterior night lighting
parameters.relationship: Artificial light at night attracts migrating birds; UBC requires Dark Sky compliant exterior lighting, which limits illuminated crowns and facade lighting; the flag feeds ECOL.

parameters.name: Facade orientation
parameters.relationship: Orientation sets solar exposure and view targets; the site plan's north arrow is skewed from the grid, so rotate to true north before assigning N/E/S/W bins.

metrics.name: WWR against reference lines
metrics.good: At or below the reference line (office 40%, hotel 34%): informational, no badge
metrics.bad: Above the reference line: judge by the ENER result, not by WWR
metrics.basis: [proxy] ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G baseline WWR is the reference model's value for performance comparison, not a limit; PNNL Table 30 column read by inference. Shown as reference lines only.
metrics.method: Glazing area divided by gross wall area, by orientation and overall

metrics.name: Envelope energy result against City energy and emissions metrics (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI)
metrics.good: At or below the VBBL limit for the occupancy, read from the by-law once opened (no number here)
metrics.basis: [unverified] VBBL 2025 (in force from 15 Sep 2025, per City guide snippet) and the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings use TEUI, TEDI and GHGI. By-law tables not read (City PDFs HTTP 403).
metrics.method: Run the EnvelopeModel in ENER; compare TEUI, TEDI and GHGI with by-law limits

metrics.name: Share of glazing treated in the bird-collision zone
metrics.good: 90% or more (UBC Tier 1, aligned with CSA)
metrics.basis: [proxy] UBC campus tiers (document read; applies to UBC, not Vancouver rezonings). CSA A460-2019 text and City Bird Friendly Design Guidelines (2017) unopened. Overhangs count up to 1:1 per UBC citing CSA.
metrics.method: (Treated glass + overhang credit) in zone divided by all glass in zone, plus all glass beside vegetation or water

metrics.name: Collision-zone height
metrics.good: Treatment to 16 m above grade or 4 m above the tallest vegetation, applied locally around each planted terrace or sky garden
metrics.basis: [proxy] UBC policy (Tiers 1-3); CSA summary says 16-25 m. Local application to sky gardens is the team's reading. City guideline match unresolved.
metrics.method: Mask facade faces below the line, using local vegetation heights from ECOL

metrics.name: Fly-through conditions and untreated glass corners
metrics.good: 0 fly-through conditions; corners treated 5 m each direction
metrics.bad: Any fly-through condition or untreated corner
metrics.basis: [proxy] UBC Backgrounder requires eliminating fly-through conditions and treating glass corners 5 m each direction in all tiers; it names CSA A460-2019 for parallel glass and corners. Standard text unopened.
metrics.method: Detect parallel or corner glass pairs with clear sight lines through the building; check corner treatment

metrics.name: Night-lighting flag (feeds ECOL)
metrics.good: Exterior lighting Dark Sky compliant; interior lights off or shielded at night
metrics.basis: [proxy] UBC Backgrounder: all exterior lighting Dark Sky compliant; interior blinds and lights-off reduce collisions. No City requirement found; LEED v5 folds bird-collision prevention into its exterior lighting credit (secondary).
metrics.method: Ask for lighting strategy per facade and crown; record answer as a judgement

metrics.name: Pattern spacing
metrics.good: Markers 50 mm or closer; linear elements 5 cm horizontal and 10 cm vertical at most; mullion subdivisions 100 x 100 mm at most
metrics.basis: [proxy] CSA summary ('2 x 2 rule', 100 x 100 mm) and UBC Backgrounder citing Klem for 5 cm and 10 cm. CSA text unopened.
metrics.method: Check the chosen pattern against spacing limits

metrics.name: Vision glazing visible light transmittance
metrics.good: 40% or more (v5: above 40%)
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] CaGBC (v4.1) and LEEDuser (v5) give 40%. CaGBC says v4.1 clarified frit and pattern wording to align with bird deterrence; v4 barred frits. Residual VLT and clarity trade-off is a judgement.
metrics.method: Read VLT from the glazing specification

metrics.name: Opaque effective U-value including thermal bridging
metrics.good: Set by the whole-building energy model against City metrics (no per-assembly threshold found)
metrics.basis: [unverified] No Vancouver per-assembly limit was opened; the City's energy limits are whole-building (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI). The BC Step Code does not apply in Vancouver.
metrics.method: Area-weighted U with psi-values and chi-values from the thermal envelope database or THERM

modules.method: 1) Rotate each face to true north and bin orientation. 2) Build glazing from the facade module or user layout; WWR by orientation, floor band and overall; draw DOE/PNNL reference lines only. 3) Bird zone: select glass below max(16 m above grade, 4 m above local vegetation) around each planted terrace or sky garden, plus all glass beside vegetation or water; treated share = (treated glass + overhang area counted up to 1:1) / glass in zone; check marker spacing. 4) Flag fly-through conditions, glass corners (5 m each direction) and exterior night lighting. 5) Check VLT of vision glazing. 6) Area-weighted effective U with psi- and chi-values. 7) Analytic shadow angles; gains from CLIM. 8) Export a facade schedule and honeybee/gbXML envelope to ENER for TEUI, TEDI and GHGI checks against the VBBL.
visualization: Unrolled four-side facade elevation: glazing, spandrel and treated glass in different fills, bold line at the local bird-zone height, red hatch on untreated zone glass and corners
Bar or radar chart of WWR by orientation with the DOE/PNNL reference line marked
Waterfall of area-weighted U-value from nominal to effective including bridging
Reference-line row linked to each source clause or table; no pass/fail badge unless the source is verified
modules.human_judgment: Facade expression, rhythm and materiality; whether to exceed reference WWR for views and light; accepting fritted glass over clear views; choice of bird-friendly product; night-lighting strategy; how the facade speaks to place and City in Nature.
modules.limits: WWR references are US baseline and prototype values, not Vancouver limits. City bird guideline, CSA A460-2019 and VBBL energy tables were not opened; UBC tiers are campus policy used as proxy. Thermal bridging needs 2D/3D modelling (THERM is free but Windows-only, not open source). Condensation, wind-driven rain, fire spread over facades and noise are not covered.

modules.name: Materials, colour and embodied carbon (material library and mood boards)
modules.design_question: Which materials, textures and colours express the project's place, what embodied carbon do they carry within a stated life-cycle scope, and how are those choices recorded and justified?
modules.effort: L (8-12 person-days); a manual-entry material library with scope-labelled kgCO2e/m2 roll-up (about 3 days) can ship earlier
inputs: P12-M06 FacadeSchedule: m2 per assembly and glazing type
STRC packet: volumes or masses of concrete, rebar, structural steel, mass timber
P12-M04: finish areas by program tag
EPD data: EC3 records via API, openEPD JSON uploads, CLF BC sourcing guide values (link, not bundled), CLF Material Baselines
User material library entries (supplier, EPD id, colour, texture, origin tag)
Mood-board images with attribution and licence
User-stated life-cycle stages, building elements and GFA basis
outputs: MaterialLibrary: typed Material {id, name, GWP, declared unit, EPD ref, stage scope, colour Lab, PBR maps, origin tag, licence}
EmbodiedCarbonReport: kgCO2e by element and per m2 GFA, always labelled with stage scope, element scope and data sources; no pass/fail badge
PaletteSpec: Lab values, lightness and contrast pairs (feeds P12-M03 reflectance, PRES style selection, renders)
DecisionRecords: judgement records for every subjective choice (feeds PRES board text and CULT review)

parameters.name: Material quantity
parameters.relationship: Embodied carbon rises in direct proportion to quantity times the EPD's GWP per declared unit; structure and facade quantities come from other modules.

parameters.name: GWP factor per declared unit
parameters.relationship: Compare at equal strength and curing age: BC 25 MPa baseline 220 kgCO2e/m3 (28 d) against Butler 109 (28 d). Heidelberg 90 is a 91-day EPD, not like-for-like. Rebar 0.85 (N. American average) to 0.44 kgCO2e/kg (Cascade).

parameters.name: Life-cycle scope and stage toggles
parameters.relationship: City scope (CLF BC webinar): A1-A5, B1-B5, C1-C4 over 60 years; structure and shell required; D and biogenic reported apart. Toggles add A4-A5, B, C (City placeholders 4, 6, 10, 5% of A1-A3). A1-A3 alone understates the total.

parameters.name: GFA basis for kgCO2e/m2
parameters.relationship: A larger GFA lowers kgCO2e/m2; the City's absolute-path slide says 'excluding parkade'. Exact wording to confirm in the guideline.

parameters.name: Data source and licence
parameters.relationship: ICE is educational-only; EC3/openEPD and CLF baselines (CC BY 4.0) can ship; the CLF BC guide shows an all-rights-reserved notice, so link to it and do not bundle its values.

parameters.name: Colour lightness (CIE L*) and reflectance
parameters.relationship: Lighter interior surfaces raise internally reflected daylight and brightness, shifting daylight reach in P12-M03; dark finishes lower it.

parameters.name: Local-material share (BC origin tag)
parameters.relationship: A higher BC share tends to cut transport emissions and supports local supply; BC EPDs are in the CLF BC guide and the naturally:wood directory. Effect size not sourced here.

parameters.name: Cultural sensitivity flag
parameters.relationship: Indigenous-related motifs, names, patterns or materials get the fixed status 'no consultation possible in this exercise'; generation and library tagging of Coast Salish motifs are blocked and the item goes to CULT as 'not proposed'.

metrics.name: Whole-building embodied carbon against City reference lines (scope-labelled)
metrics.unit: kgCO2e/m2 GFA, with stage and element scope shown
metrics.good: Scope complete (A1-C4, structure and shell) and below the reference line: shown as 'within reference', not 'pass'
metrics.bad: Scope partial: label 'A1-A3 partial; cap scope unverified' and show no comparison
metrics.basis: [legacy_version] 800 kgCO2e/m2 is the 2023 absolute limit (2 x 400), stages A-C, structure and shell (CLF BC webinar, secondary). 2025 proposal: 360; adoption unconfirmed; VBBL text unopened.
metrics.method: Sum quantity x GWP over in-scope elements divided by GFA; compare only when the scope matches

metrics.name: Reduction against baseline (2025 proposal)
metrics.good: 10% below baseline (5-10% whole-building plus 0-5% industry-leadership credits) for Part 3 buildings over 1,800 m2
metrics.basis: [unverified] City/CLF BC workshop slides (May 2024) show the revised proposal; the 2022 scheme gave 20% for 1-6 storey wood and 10% for others. Whether VBBL 2025 adopted it is unconfirmed.
metrics.method: 1 - (project / baseline), baseline per the City's Embodied Carbon Guidelines

metrics.name: GWP per material against best like-for-like BC EPD
metrics.good: At or near the lowest like-for-like EPD: concrete 25 MPa 109 kgCO2e/m3 (Butler, 28 d); rebar 0.44 kgCO2e/kg (Cascade)
metrics.bad: Above the BC industry baseline: concrete 220/259/294 kgCO2e/m3 at 25/30/35 MPa; rebar 0.85
metrics.basis: [verified] CLF BC Low-Carbon Material Sourcing Guide (updated 9 Feb 2026), EC3 GWP, A1-A3 only, glass not covered. Copyright notice all rights reserved: link, do not bundle.
metrics.method: Lookup by material, strength and curing age; compare project choice

metrics.name: Embodied-carbon data source eligibility
metrics.good: EC3 / openEPD EPDs or CLF baselines (CC BY 4.0); ICE only as user-supplied data in teaching mode
metrics.bad: ICE bundled or used for non-educational project calculations
metrics.basis: ICE Database Educational V5.0 (June 2026) is educational-only; tools, software, reporting and project calculations are excluded; non-educational use not permitted from 30 Sept 2026.
metrics.method: Per-record licence field checked before export

metrics.name: Interior surface lightness
metrics.good: User-set target; no sourced threshold
metrics.basis: [unverified] Accessibility contrast values (for example CSA B651 light-reflectance difference) were not opened.
metrics.method: Convert sRGB to CIELAB; lightness and CIEDE2000 between adjacent surfaces

metrics.name: Indigenous-related items with fixed 'no consultation possible' status
metrics.good: 100% carry the fixed status, are not generated, and board text says no consultation took place
metrics.bad: Any item claims consultation or is generated
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Entrants are anonymous, have weeks and no relationship with the Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh Nations, so a consultation record would be false. Tool rule.
metrics.method: Scan library and mood-board items tagged Indigenous-related; check status and routing to CULT

metrics.name: Decision-record completeness
metrics.unit: % of palette and material choices with rationale, author, source and licence
metrics.good: 100% (tool rule)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Team rule for the course requirement that results cite sources and separate delegated from human judgement.
metrics.method: Count records with all required fields

modules.method: Objective part: embodied carbon = sum of quantity x GWP per declared unit over in-scope elements, divided by GFA. Default A1-A3 from EC3/openEPD records, CLF BC guide values or CLF baselines with a data-quality flag; the user ticks stages A4-A5, B, C (Brightway or City placeholders) and elements, and the report always prints that scope. No pass/fail badge: reference lines (800 legacy, 360 proposed) show only when scope is A-C, structure and shell. ICE is blocked outside teaching mode. Subjective part: each library item and mood-board image carries source, licence, colour (sRGB to CIELAB), PBR maps (CC0), origin tag and a decision record (author, date, alternatives, rationale, jury criteria, status). Indigenous-related items get the fixed status and are not generated. Palettes are clustered and checked with CIEDE2000.
visualization: Stacked bar of kgCO2e/m2 by element (structure, envelope, interiors) with a scope label and reference lines only when scope matches
Lollipop chart per material: project choice versus lowest like-for-like BC EPD and BC baseline
Palette swatch strip with Lab values and lightness, plus contrast pairs
Material cards with provenance badges (EPD id, source, licence) and PBR preview
Mood-board grid with captions, attributions and linked decision records
modules.human_judgment: All palette, mood, texture, tectonic and symbolic choices; what 'City in Nature' means materially; whether to use local timber or stone; Indigenous-informed expression is not proposed because no consultation is possible here; trade-offs between embodied carbon, durability, cost and expression; which life-cycle scope to state.
modules.limits: EPD coverage has gaps (glass not in the CLF BC guide; much BC rebar is imported). GWP varies by plant and year. The by-law's current scope, 2025 text and guideline version were not read; the City's PDFs returned HTTP 403. VTC is an ideas competition, so VBBL and policy values serve only as benchmarks. EC3 API terms not opened. Screen colour differs from built colour.

modules.name: Interior comfort: thermal, acoustic and supertall-specific (roadmap)
modules.design_question: Will typical interior zones be thermally, acoustically and physically comfortable given the envelope, occupancy, adjacencies, finishes and the wind and stack effects of a 300 m tower?
inputs: ENER EnergyPlus results: zone air and radiant temperatures by hour
P12-M06 envelope properties and window areas
P12-M04 occupancy and activity (metabolic rate proxy)
P12-M05 adjacency pairs and noise sources
STRC: peak wind-induced acceleration by floor and return period
SYST: stack-effect pressure differences across doors and shafts, lift noise
Finish absorption data (not yet in the material library)
outputs: ComfortReport: PMV/PPD or adaptive comfort by zone and hour; hours outside the range
AcousticRequirementMatrix: required sound isolation per adjacent pair (feeds P12-M05, P12-M06 glazing, P12-M07 finishes)
MotionAndPressureFlags: floors where reported acceleration or door pressure exceeds the criterion chosen (values from STRC and SYST)

parameters.name: Operative temperature, air speed, humidity, clothing, metabolic rate
parameters.relationship: These set PMV; the CBE tool and pythermalcomfort compute PMV and PPD from them under ASHRAE 55, ISO 7730 and EN 16798.

parameters.name: Glazing U and WWR on a perimeter zone
parameters.relationship: Colder window surfaces lower mean radiant temperature in winter and increase radiant asymmetry near glazing; higher SHGC raises it in summer (physical relationship, simulated by ENER).

parameters.name: Radiant asymmetry and downdraft at full-height glazing
parameters.relationship: Cold glass drives downdraft and asymmetric radiation on occupants near it; stronger glazing, perimeter heating or a larger setback reduce both. ASHRAE 55 limits not read; no numbers.

parameters.name: Perceived wind-induced building motion (residential, hotel floors)
parameters.unit: peak acceleration, milli-g, with return period
parameters.relationship: Higher upper-floor acceleration raises motion perception and discomfort; stiffer structure or damping lowers it. ISO 10137 is the standard to open; no numbers until read; value from STRC.

parameters.name: Stack-effect pressure across doors and shafts
parameters.relationship: A tall building's stack effect raises door-opening force, can stop lift doors closing and cause whistling and draughts at doors; vestibules and compartmentation lower it. Values from SYST.

parameters.name: Sound isolation between adjacent uses
parameters.relationship: Higher required isolation between a noisy use (venue, plant) and a quiet one (hotel, dwelling) increases slab and wall mass and affects stacking in P12-M05.

parameters.name: Finish absorption and reverberation
parameters.relationship: Hard finishes raise reverberation time and background speech level in open spaces; absorptive ceilings lower them. Needs finish data not yet in the library.

parameters.name: Exterior noise at the arterial street, and lift and wind noise
parameters.relationship: Higher street, lift-shaft or wind noise raises the glazing and facade sound-reduction needed, linking back to P12-M06 and SYST.

metrics.name: PMV comfort band
metrics.good: Between -0.5 and +0.5
metrics.basis: [verified_secondary] CBE Thermal Comfort Tool states the comfort zone is PMV -0.5 to +0.5 according to ASHRAE 55; standard text unopened.
metrics.method: pythermalcomfort PMV/PPD per zone and hour

metrics.name: Hours outside the comfort band
metrics.good: Set by the team (no sourced limit)
metrics.basis: [unverified] No VBBL or ASHRAE hour-count limit opened; the CBE tool reports 80% and 90% acceptability limits for adaptive comfort.
metrics.method: Count occupied hours with |PMV| above 0.5

metrics.name: Peak wind-induced acceleration against occupant-motion criterion
metrics.good: At or below the criterion the STRC wind engineer adopts from ISO 10137 or a named alternative (no number given)
metrics.basis: [unverified] ISO 10137:2007 covers serviceability against vibration; Annex D wind-motion limits, ISO 6897 and any other criterion were not read.
metrics.method: Read STRC acceleration by floor; compare with the chosen criterion

metrics.name: Stack-effect door pressure difference
metrics.good: At or below the door-operation limit SYST adopts (no number given)
metrics.basis: [unverified] A 1968 ASHRAE paper and a 2025 thesis describe stack-effect door and elevator problems; neither opened and no limit read.
metrics.method: Read SYST pressure differences by floor and door type

metrics.name: Sound isolation between adjacent dwellings or hotel rooms
metrics.good: Value from the Vancouver Building By-law (not opened)
metrics.basis: [unverified] Acoustic limits in VBBL 2025, WELL and ISO 3382-3 were not opened; BCBC does not apply in Vancouver. No numbers until read.
metrics.method: Lookup by assembly

modules.method: 1) Read hourly zone results from the ENER EnergyPlus run, including operative temperature, mean radiant temperature and humidity. 2) Compute PMV and PPD with pythermalcomfort for each zone-hour, using schedules and metabolic and clothing presets from P12-M04; use the adaptive method where windows are operable. 3) Report hours outside the comfort band by zone and orientation; flag perimeter zones for radiant asymmetry and downdraft. 4) Read STRC wind-motion and SYST stack-effect results and compare with criteria chosen by those packets. 5) Acoustics (later): for each adjacent pair in P12-M05, look up required isolation, compare with assembly ratings, and use an image-source simulation for reverberation. 6) Return requirements to P12-M05, P12-M06 and P12-M07.
visualization: Zone x hour heat map of PMV on a diverging scale with the +/-0.5 band marked
Plan coloured by hours outside the comfort band, perimeter zones highlighted
Tower elevation with acceleration and door-pressure flags by floor (values from STRC and SYST)
Acoustic adjacency matrix with required versus provided isolation
modules.human_judgment: What comfort and quiet mean for each program (lively civic hall versus hotel room); window-opening policy; accepting wider temperature swings for lower energy; which motion criterion suits residential and hotel floors; occupant surveys and post-occupancy feedback.
modules.limits: Depends on ENER, STRC and SYST outputs and finish data that do not exist yet. Local discomfort limits, motion criteria and acoustic limits were not read, so no thresholds are given. Occupant adaptation is not covered. Roadmap only.

modules.name: Evidence-status and badge consistency gate
modules.design_question: Does every metric's pass/fail badge match what its source supports, and does each status agree with the flags register?
depends_on: All P12 metric records (status, source_ids, opened flag)
inputs: Metric records: status, status_detail, source_ids
Source records: type (primary or secondary), opened, edition currency
Flags register: FALSE_ASSUMPTION, UNVERIFIED, UNRESOLVED, TEAM_ASSUMPTION
outputs: BadgeDecision per metric: show pass/fail, reference line only, or hide
ConsistencyReport: metrics whose status contradicts a flag, a source flag or a missing source id

parameters.name: Status vocabulary (verified, verified_secondary, proxy, legacy_version, team_assumption, unverified, false_assumption_corrected)
parameters.relationship: Only 'verified' (current official text opened) unlocks a pass/fail badge; every other status renders a labelled reference line, so a user cannot read a proxy as a compliance result.

parameters.name: Source opened flag and source type
parameters.relationship: A source with opened = false can never support 'verified'; a secondary source caps status at verified_secondary, so a trade-press summary cannot produce a badge.

parameters.name: Edition currency (in force, superseded, proposed)
parameters.relationship: A threshold from a superseded or proposed edition is tagged legacy_version and cannot show a badge, which stops v4 LEED or 2023 embodied-carbon limits appearing as current tests.

metrics.name: Pass/fail badges shown on non-verified metrics
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Tool rule from the course requirement to cite sources, show work and separate what code, AI and people decide; raised in critique round 1.
metrics.method: Scan metric records: status != verified and badge rendered

metrics.name: Metrics whose status contradicts a flag or source record
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Round 1 found 'verified' metrics with UNVERIFIED flags, unopened sources or superseded editions.
metrics.method: Join metrics to flags and sources; report mismatches

metrics.name: Metrics without a source id (excluding team presets)
metrics.basis: [team_assumption] Every threshold must be verified, a team assumption or unverified, with a source record where one exists.
metrics.method: Count metrics with empty source_ids and status other than team_assumption

modules.method: On every build, load all metric, source and flag records. Rule 1: status 'verified' requires every cited source to have opened = true, be primary, and be the edition in force; otherwise downgrade and tag verified_secondary, proxy or legacy_version. Rule 2: a metric cited by an UNVERIFIED or FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag cannot be 'verified'. Rule 3: badge state follows status (verified: pass/fail; others: labelled reference line). Rule 4: report mismatches and block export of boards until zero remain or a judgement record explains the exception.
visualization: Table of metrics by status with badge state; red row when status and flag disagree
Counts of metrics per status by module
modules.human_judgment: Whether a secondary source is acceptable for a reference line; who may promote a metric to 'verified' after opening the official text; which exceptions to allow.
modules.limits: Checks only the records, not whether a cited source says what the record claims; a human must still open the source.
