flags.correction: ICE Database Educational V5.0 (June 2026) is educational-only; software, tools, reporting and project calculations are excluded and non-educational use is no longer permitted from 30 Sept 2026. Use EC3/openEPD EPDs and CLF baselines (CC BY 4.0); ICE only as user-supplied data in teaching mode.
flags.detail: Raised from the packet scope text 'EC3/ICE'. Source P12-S27. EC3 is labelled free and open access, but API terms and rate limits were not read (P12-S28, P12-S29).

flags.claim: Vancouver's older view-cone policy with 38 cones, including Queen Elizabeth Park cones 3.1 and 3.2.4a, is still in force.
flags.correction: On 10 July 2024 Council repealed it and adopted Public Views Guidelines with 24 cones; Queen Elizabeth Park 3.2.1-3.2.4 remain, 3.1 and 3.2.4a were removed. The Higher Buildings Policy Review says protected views are not being reviewed.
flags.detail: Facts come from a news article (P12-S01) and the review page (P12-S03); the official guidelines PDF returned HTTP 403 (P12-S02). Verify cone numbers in VanMap before citing on boards.

flags.claim: BC Building Code 2024 (occupant loads, separations, acoustics) and the BC Energy Step Code govern a tower in downtown Vancouver.
flags.correction: The City of Vancouver has its own building by-law. Use the Vancouver Building By-law (2025 edition, in force from 15 Sep 2025 per City guide snippets) and the City's energy and emissions metrics (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI), values unverified until read.
flags.detail: Province page (P12-S21), re-opened in r1: 'BC Codes don't apply in the City of Vancouver which has its own building bylaw.' VBBL 2025 itself (P12-S49) returned HTTP 403; every BCBC reference and 'Step Code' export was replaced.

flags.claim: No source resolves how bird-friendly patterned glass and LEED view glazing can both be satisfied.
flags.correction: CaGBC says the LEED v4.1 addenda clarified frit and pattern wording to align with bird-collision deterrence; the LEEDuser v5 page says frits, patterns or tints must preserve the view. Only the VLT and view-clarity trade-off remains, as a judgement.
flags.detail: Sources P12-S05 (opened r1) and P12-S56. Official v4.1 and v5 credit text not opened; the allowed frit or pattern density is not stated.

flags.claim: LEED v4/v4.1 credit thresholds (EQc7 sDA/ASE, EQc8 views) are the current LEED benchmark.
flags.correction: LEED v5 (April 2025 launch edition) is available for BD+C. Label v4 and v4.1 values legacy_version; v5 values come from a secondary page (LEEDuser) and stay unverified until the USGBC text is opened.
flags.detail: P12-S57 (USGBC v5 page, opened) and P12-S56 (LEEDuser v5 EQc2). v5 moves views, daylight, thermal and sound into Occupant Experience; bird-collision prevention moves into exterior lighting (P12-S58, snippet).

flags.claim: Turner et al. (2001) report only qualitative correspondence between visibility-graph measures and use.
flags.correction: The paper reports an exponential fit (R2 = 0.63) between observed Tate Gallery room occupancy and mean shortest path length. It is evidence for relative use in one building, not a threshold.
flags.detail: P12-S10 re-read in r1 (Fig. 13); the paper itself also says 'qualitative correspondence' for movement patterns and 'some quantitative correspondence' in its conclusion.

flags.claim: EN 17037 view-out levels are an area-share criterion ('% of area by EN 17037 level').
flags.correction: The standard's view-out methods are point-in-space assessments (Annex C). Report per-point levels; the area share is a ClimateStudio-style convention and is labelled so.
flags.detail: REHVA Journal (P12-S07) says view out methods refer to point-in-space assessments; ClimateStudio docs (P12-S08) summarise results as a percentage of regularly occupied floor area.

flags.claim: BC 25 MPa concrete ranges from 220 to 90 kgCO2e/m3 (like-for-like), and CLF BC guide values can be used as open data.
flags.correction: The 90 figure is a 91-day EPD and the 220 baseline is at 28 days; compare Butler 109 (28 d) with 220. The guide carries an all-rights-reserved notice and no licence, so link to it and do not bundle its values.
flags.detail: P12-S25: Heidelberg 90 at 91 d, Butler 109 at 28 d, '(c) 2026 ZEIC All Rights Reserved'.

flags.claim: An A1-A3 embodied-carbon sum can be tested pass/fail against Vancouver's 800 kgCO2e/m2 cap.
flags.correction: 800 is the City's 2023 absolute limit over stages A-C (60 years) for structure and shell, so an A1-A3 sum is a partial scope. A 10% reduction (360 absolute) was proposed for 2025; adoption is unconfirmed. Show scope-labelled reference lines, no badge.
flags.detail: Scope from the CLF BC webinar on City guidelines v1.0 (P12-S53) and workshop slides (P12-S52); official guidelines and VBBL 2025 text unopened (HTTP 403).

flags.claim: The ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G baseline WWR (office 40%, hotel 34%) is a limit that a facade must stay under.
flags.correction: It is the reference model's WWR used for performance comparison. Show 40% and 34% only as reference lines (proxy) and judge the facade by the ENER result against the City's TEDI, TEUI and GHGI.
flags.detail: P12-S18 (PNNL TSD Table 30, column read by inference). A prescriptive 90.1 WWR cap was not opened and is not a Vancouver requirement.

flags.claim: A visibility-graph partition can have fractional transparency (0 to 1).
flags.correction: A visibility edge exists or not. Use binary flags (opaque, glazed, open) and two graphs: visibility at eye height, accessibility at floor height with glass as a barrier, as Turner et al. built for the Barcelona Pavilion.
flags.detail: P12-S10 (Barcelona Pavilion 0.5 m grid, eye-height and floor-height graphs).

flags.claim: A net-to-gross factor can be applied to DOE/PNNL densities and the energy 'design' population can size lifts.
flags.correction: PNNL densities are per zone floor area, so efficiency applies only to net-basis densities. Lifts use their own vertical-transportation basis; egress uses the VBBL table and 2 persons per sleeping area, not DOE 2.5 per unit.
flags.detail: P12-S19 (zone area basis), P12-S51 (VBBL 2019 Part 9 sleeping-area rule), P12-S62 (lift-planning densities, secondary).

flags.claim: Competition entrants can record Indigenous consultation status as obtained or in progress.
flags.correction: Entrants are anonymous, have weeks and no relationship with the Musqueam, Squamish or Tsleil-Waututh Nations. The fixed status is 'no consultation possible in this exercise'; motif generation is blocked and items go to CULT as 'not proposed'.
flags.detail: P12-S48 (anonymous judging, 30 Nov 2026 deadline). A consultation field could invite a false claim on boards.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver Bird Friendly Design Guidelines (2015, amended May 2017) set a numeric glazing-treatment zone and spacing.
flags.correction: Not confirmed. The City PDF returned HTTP 403. UBC tiers (P12-S31) and a CSA summary (P12-S32) are used as proxies and flagged.
flags.detail: UBC's policy applies to the UBC campus, not Vancouver rezonings. CSA A460-2019 text (P12-S59) not opened.

flags.claim: VBBL 2025 Part 3 Table 3.1.17.1 occupant load factors (office recalled as 9.3 m2 per person) and the sleeping-room rule.
flags.correction: Not confirmed. The VBBL 2025 PDF returned HTTP 403. VBBL 2019 Part 9 text says 2 persons per bedroom or sleeping area; the Part 3 wording and area basis must be read.
flags.detail: The M04 egress metric depends on it (P12-S49, P12-S51). BCBC no longer cited.

flags.claim: ASHRAE 90.1 prescriptive path caps vertical glazing at 40% of gross wall area.
flags.correction: Not confirmed; only DOE/PNNL prototype and Appendix G baseline WWR were read (P12-S18).
flags.detail: Vancouver towers are judged against the City's energy and emissions limits in the VBBL, so a hard WWR cap may not apply.

flags.claim: Vancouver embodied carbon limit is 800 kgCO2e/m2, with a 10% reduction from 2025 for a supertall.
flags.correction: 800 is the 2023 limit (A-C stages, structure and shell). The 10% reduction (360 absolute) is a 2024 revised proposal for Part 3 buildings over 1,800 m2; whether VBBL 2025 adopted it, and the guideline version, are unconfirmed.
flags.detail: P12-S52, P12-S53, P12-S54 are secondary; City PDFs unopened (P12-S46, P12-S49, P12-S55). The Policy bulletin snippet says rezonings show readiness for VBBL limits at first Building Permit.

flags.claim: LEED v5 view, daylight and glare criteria as quoted by LEEDuser apply as written.
flags.correction: Only LEEDuser (secondary) and a USGBC overview were opened; the USGBC credit text was not. The LEEDuser page is internally inconsistent on Option 5 points.
flags.detail: P12-S56, P12-S57. Check USGBC v5 text before any badge; v4/v4.1 values stay legacy_version.

flags.claim: VBBL 2025 energy and emissions limits (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI) by occupancy for Part 3 towers.
flags.correction: Not read. City PDFs returned HTTP 403 and the 2019/2021 primer (P12-S66) was not opened; no numbers are given and ENER results show without a limit line.
flags.detail: P12-M06 envelope energy metric.

flags.claim: CIBSE Guide D (2025) office population densities and five-minute handling capacities.
flags.correction: Not opened. A wiki summary (P12-S62) gives 10/14/19 m2 per person and 15% historic versus 7% suggested; treat as secondary reference points.
flags.detail: P12-M04 vertical-transportation basis.

flags.claim: ISO 10137 and other criteria for perceived wind-induced motion, and ASHRAE 55 radiant asymmetry and stack-effect door limits.
flags.correction: Sources named, none read; no numbers are given.
flags.detail: P12-M08 roadmap parameters (P12-S64, P12-S65, P12-S67, P12-S68).

flags.claim: HRDEM covers the North Shore ridgelines at usable resolution.
flags.correction: The dataset page says coverage is still being established and gives no regional list.
flags.detail: P12-S40; check the footprint files, otherwise use a coarser DEM or manual ridgeline.

flags.claim: Goia (2016) gives an optimal WWR range for offices.
flags.correction: Only the citation was confirmed; the abstract and results were not read, and the study covers European climates.

flags.claim: Acoustic thresholds (STC between dwellings or hotel rooms, open-plan speech metrics).
flags.correction: Not read from VBBL, WELL or ISO 3382-3; no numbers are given.
flags.detail: P12-M08 acoustic metric is unverified.

flags.claim: EN 17037 'layers seen' criterion.
flags.correction: REHVA gives layer counts 1/2/3; ClimateStudio says minimum requires the landscape layer, medium landscape plus one, high all three.
flags.detail: Standard text not opened; P12-M02 shows counts and notes the nuance.

flags.claim: Residual trade-off between bird-friendly pattern density and view clarity or VLT.
flags.correction: The frit and pattern wording is aligned with bird deterrence in v4.1 and v5 summaries (see FALSE_ASSUMPTION above); the allowed density and the visual effect on a 300 m tower's views are not stated.
flags.detail: Recorded as a human judgement in P12-M06.

flags.claim: Floor-area definition and Vancouver floor-area exclusions for the 9.0 FSR non-residential test.
flags.correction: The competition brief's definition and the citywide Zoning and Development By-law exclusions were not read; site by-laws often exclude below-grade parking and sometimes mechanical space (snippets only).
flags.detail: P12-S48, P12-S69. The tool shows strict and inclusive FSR and defaults to excluding mechanical, core and below-grade.

flags.claim: EN 17037 view-out levels and LEED view tests are the benchmark for view access in a Vancouver tower.
flags.correction: No BC or Vancouver view-out standard was found. EN 17037 is European and LEED a voluntary credit; both are editable benchmarks.

flags.claim: Daylight-zone depth equals 2.0 x window head height, as a lighting-control proxy.
flags.correction: Mirrors ASHRAE 90.1 primary plus secondary sidelighted areas (draft text, unopened); Reinhart (2005) abstract supports the head-height rule for standard variants. Replace with simulated sDA from CLIM.

flags.claim: Isovist and VGA good/bad is judged by quartiles of the project's own results, with 80% and 50% visibility cut-offs for entries.
flags.correction: No published absolute thresholds were found; Turner et al. (2001) interpret measures relatively.

flags.claim: Occupancy is kept in four bases (egress, design, energy, vertical transportation) with attendance factor 1.0 by default and 1.0 always for egress.
flags.correction: A design decision to avoid hiding the difference between code loads, typical use and lift demand; the default 1.0 avoids inventing an unsourced hybrid-work reduction.

flags.claim: The hypothetical site occupies a georeferenced proxy block supplied by the SITE packet, and target views are derived from it.
flags.correction: Site-plan labels (Stanley Park, BC Place, North Shore Mountains) are directions, not points. Every target result is conditional on the proxy and shown with a sensitivity range.
flags.detail: P12-M02. The SITE packet must record the proxy choice and rotation range.

flags.claim: VBBL, Green Buildings Policy and LEED values are used as benchmarks, not compliance tests, for an ideas competition.
flags.correction: VTC is not a rezoning or permit application; the brief says its documents are not legal documents. Thresholds are editable reference lines.
flags.detail: All P12 modules; P12-X01 enforces badge rules.

flags.claim: The 9.0 FSR test counts only office and retail/commercial area by default; hotel and cultural/civic count by recorded toggle.
flags.correction: The brief wording 'non-residential, high-employment (office, commercial)' is the team's summary; inclusive counts are shown separately and never replace the strict count.
flags.detail: P12-M04; brief PDF not opened (P12-S48).

unresolved_relationships: Quantitative relationship between plan depth, window head height and daylight penetration (the k in k x head height): ASHRAE 90.1 sidelighted-area text and Reinhart (2005) abstract seen, tabulated factors and full text not opened.

How isovist and VGA measures relate to perceived legibility, wayfinding and use in supertall podiums and sky lobbies: Turner et al. (2001) show an exponential fit (R2 = 0.63) of room occupancy to mean shortest path length in one gallery; no thresholds and no supertall evidence.
Relationship between floor height, mountain or water view and rent premium in Vancouver towers: no source found.
How target-view results change with the assumed georeferenced proxy block and rotation for the hypothetical site: depends on the SITE packet's choice; sensitivity runs report the range.

Quantitative effect of WWR on total energy in Vancouver's climate: Goia (2016) covers European climates and was not read; a project-specific ENER model against the City's TEUI, TEDI and GHGI is needed.
How bird-friendly frit or pattern density trades against view clarity and VLT for LEED v4.1/v5 and the City of Vancouver: wording is aligned in summaries, allowed density not stated.
Effect of hybrid work and desk sharing on peak and average office occupancy and lift demand in downtown Vancouver: no source opened; CIBSE Guide D (2025) not opened.
Net-to-gross efficiency by use for supertall mixed-use towers in Vancouver: no sourced values found.
Basis for numeric weights in the A/E/I/O/U/X adjacency scale and for public-continuity limits: the scale is qualitative; Muther's primary text not opened; no calibration found.
Plate or lease depth, floor-to-floor height and stack alignment effects on stacking by use: no sourced ranges; values must come from SYST/STRC.
Fire separation and sound isolation required between major occupancies in the Vancouver Building By-law 2025: not read (City PDFs HTTP 403).
VBBL 2025 Part 3 occupant-load table, its area basis (net or gross) and the sleeping-room rule: Part 9 2019 text read only.

Life-cycle stages, elements, GFA basis and reduction factor of Vancouver's embodied carbon requirement as adopted in VBBL 2025, and its interaction with the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings: official texts not opened; a 10% reduction (360 absolute) was proposed.
VBBL 2025 energy and emissions limits (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI) by occupancy for Part 3 towers: not read.
Floor-area definition and exclusions that govern the 9.0 FSR non-residential test: competition brief and citywide by-law not read.
Accessibility colour-contrast (light reflectance value) thresholds applicable in BC (for example CSA B651): not opened.
Whether City of Vancouver's Bird Friendly Design Guidelines (2017) use the same collision-zone height (16 m) and spacing as CSA and UBC: City PDF HTTP 403; CSA A460-2019 text not opened.

Perceived wind-induced motion criteria (ISO 10137 Annex D, ISO 6897 or others) for residential and hotel floors near 300 m, radiant asymmetry and downdraft limits at full-height glazing, and stack-effect door forces: sources named, none read.

Missing from this packet and routed to other packets: visual privacy and overlook between towers, interior biophilia and sky gardens (ECOL), balcony and winter-garden wind policy, universal design and wayfinding signage.

Schema gap: the module-metric status enum lacks verified_secondary, proxy and legacy_version; they are carried in status_detail and a bracket tag at the start of basis (proxy maps to team_assumption; verified_secondary and legacy_version map to unverified) until the orchestrator extends the enum.
change_log: Round 1 (21 Oct 2026): first specification of packet P12 with 8 modules (M01 isovist/VGA, M02 view access, M03 depth from glazing, M04 occupancy and schedules, M05 adjacency and stacking, M06 facade and envelope, M07 materials, colour and embodied carbon, M08 comfort).

Corrected the packet scope's 'embodied carbon via EC3/ICE': ICE Educational V5.0 is educational-only and non-educational use ends 30 Sept 2026, so EC3/openEPD and CLF data are the tool defaults (FALSE_ASSUMPTION recorded).
Corrected view-protection assumptions: the old view-cone policy was replaced by Public Views Guidelines on 10 July 2024 (FALSE_ASSUMPTION recorded, from a secondary source).
Split 'depth from glazing' (P12-M03) from 'view access' (P12-M02) because they use different thresholds and priorities.

Replaced remembered numbers with team_assumption or unverified labels wherever the source could not be opened (occupant load, ASHRAE WWR cap, acoustic limits, daylight k factor).

notes:
r1 revision of P12 after independent critique. Governing code corrected to the Vancouver Building By-law (2025 edition, in force 15 Sep 2025 per City guide snippets) in place of BCBC and the Step Code; its tables could not be read (City PDFs HTTP 403) and the web-search budget ran out during this round, so VBBL values stay unverified. PDFs fetched by the tool (CLF BC slides, UBC backgrounder, Turner et al., VBBL 2019 s.9.9) were decoded to stdout only; no files were created.

Status mapping (the schema enum has four values): verified = current official text opened; unverified = sourced but secondary, legacy or unread (tags verified_secondary, legacy_version carried in status_detail and as a bracket tag in basis); team_assumption = team preset or proxy; false_assumption_corrected = corrected claim. Pass/fail badges only for 'verified'; the new gate P12-X01 enforces this. Only the CLF BC material guide values and the ICE correction use verified or corrected status.

Objective versus subjective is unchanged: geometry, ray casting, graph measures, population arithmetic and kgCO2e sums are objective; adjacency ratings, palette, view weights, public/private visibility and every team_assumption threshold are judgements saved as JudgementRecords. Indigenous-related items are never generated and always carry 'no consultation possible in this exercise'.

Dates and priorities: core for 13 Nov 2026 is M04, the M06 WWR and bird-zone cut and P12-X01; v1 by 10 Dec 2026 is M01, M02 (first slice), M03, M05, M07; M08 is roadmap. The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy still governs; the brief says its documents are not legal documents, so all thresholds are benchmarks.
